editorialRead.readHeadline: aaif-goose/goose is the first source to inspect.
editorialRead.oneLineSummary: aaif-goose/goose leads a 3-item attention queue backed by direct receipts; 24 watchlist sources are fresh, 0 need source-health attention, and movement still requires editorial judgment.
editorialRead.dek: Agent Pulse filtered 24 included projects down to 3 items worth finite newsroom attention. The queue protects attention; it does not declare winners.
bullets: aaif-goose/goose — 2 commits today and 2 same-day mapped articles, 5.9 below its current daily pace, with 1 hardening-subject points. Inspect the receipt before assigning a story.
NousResearch/hermes-agent — 116 commits landed today. Keep it on watch, but require the next receipt to prove a reader consequence before promoting it.
different-ai/openwork — No same-day commit after 209 commits in the seven-day window. The pause is notable enough to preserve, not enough to turn into a story.
editorialRead.watchNext: The next meaningful upgrade is feedback flow: issues opened and closed, review latency, stale backlog, and the share of work that starts outside the maintainer team.
editorialRead.caveat: Source-code motion and article coverage are collected. GitHub issue flow, PR review timing, community discussion, and private backlog signals are not.

dailyInsight.headline: A new model route should trigger a permission-mode audit
dailyInsight.insight: Goose's public Claude Opus 5 change adds provider mappings and an adaptive-thinking request test, while its permission documentation keeps autonomy as a separate operator choice. Treat a model addition as a reason to verify the local-action boundary, not as a reason to assume the boundary stayed understood.
dailyInsight.mechanism: The inspected commit updates Goose's canonical model data, Anthropic request formatting, and focused tests for the Claude 5 adaptive-thinking shape. Separately, Goose documents Autonomous, Manual Approval, Smart Approval, and Chat Only modes; its public permission inspector has distinct paths for explicit policy, read-only classification, extension management, and unknown tools.
dailyInsight.whyItMatters: A model compatibility update can change the intelligence at the center of an agent without changing the tools around it. If that agent can use MCP extensions and local developer tools, the useful safety question is whether the operator can still explain which actions need confirmation, rather than whether the new model name appears in a picker.

actions.label: Audit one model-to-tool path
actions.instruction: In a non-sensitive workspace, select the intended Goose permission mode, enable only one known extension, and run a bounded task with the newly mapped model. Record which tool calls proceed, which ask for approval, and how an unfamiliar tool is handled before granting the model broader access.

actions.label: Keep compatibility and authority tests separate
actions.instruction: When adding a provider or model family, test the request-format contract independently from permission behavior. Exercise explicit allow, deny, unknown-tool, extension-management, and read-only paths so a passing provider test cannot stand in for an authority audit.

receipts.title: chore: opus5 support (including adaptive thinking) (#10686)
receipts.supports: Shows canonical Claude Opus 5 mappings across provider identities, adaptive-thinking request formatting, and focused source tests that anchor this project-scoped compatibility call.

receipts.title: Goose Permission Modes
receipts.supports: Shows that Goose publicly separates Autonomous, Manual Approval, Smart Approval, and Chat Only modes, with Autonomous documented as the default operator posture.

confidence.basis: The fresh public commit, inspected formatter and regression test, permission documentation, and permission-inspector source agree that provider compatibility and tool authority are distinct Goose control surfaces.

dailyInsight.limitation: This is source-level Goose evidence. It does not establish a release, a working provider account, the behavior of every extension, or the correctness of all permission classifications in a deployed session.
dailyInsight.falsifier: Revise this call if the provider mapping is reverted, if a public release changes the documented default or mode semantics, or if later source or tests show that a supported extension path bypasses the stated permission controls.
dailyInsight.watchNext: Watch for a Goose release and a public end-to-end test that pairs a newly mapped provider with a local extension under each permission mode, including an unknown-tool and denied-action path.
